title: Echoes From the Void: Detecting DNS Tunneling With Blackhole Features in Encrypted Scenarios With High Accuracy

value.quote: Experiments were conducted using the GraphTunnel data set (2,975,353 records) and the CIC-Bell-DNS-E

datasets_evaluated.evidence: Experiments were conducted using the GraphTunnel data set (2,975,353 records) and the CIC-Bell-DNS-EXF-2021 (1,019,318 records).

label_source.evidence: The formatted dataset comprises 1,019,318 samples based on the raw DNS traffic of 270.8 MB and is classified as: • Heavy Attack Samples: 323,698 samples of highbandwidth aggressive DNS tunneling

label_feature_overlap.evidence: The extracted features were placed in an ordered dataframe and labeled as either benign or tunnel.

features_used.evidence: We engineered a set of seventeen features, comprising eleven traditional DNS traffic metrics and six novel blackhole-based features.

feature_groups.evidence: We engineered a set of seventeen features, comprising eleven traditional DNS traffic metrics and six novel blackhole-based features.

cert_fields_read.evidence: The system does not inspect the payload, so it works with a lightweight mechanism even under encrypted DNS traffic

model_family.value: random forest, XGBoost, CNN, LSTM, SVM, voting ensemble
model_family.evidence: The chosen classifiers are: Random forest, XGBoost, Convolutional neural network (CNN), Long short-term memory (LSTM), Support vector machine (SVM), Voting ensemble (combining RF, XGBoost, and CNN).

split_protocols.evidence: We randomly divided the data into training and testing sets using an 80/20 stratified split to preserve class balance.

main_split.evidence: We randomly divided the data into training and testing sets using an 80/20 stratified split to preserve class balance.

easy_vs_hard_reported.evidence: All measures were computed on each experiment’s heldout test set using stratified 80/20 splits.

shortcut_check.evidence: To analyze the contribution of each feature, we conducted an ablation study by iteratively eliminating one feature at a time from the complete combined set

metrics.evidence: Classification accuracy was examined using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.

granularity.evidence: A single feature vector exists per PCAP file that enables scalable analysis for several DNS sessions.

first_n_packets.evidence: each packet is broken down to extract both classic and novel behavioral features, aggregating at the PCAP session level.

cost_reported.evidence: our random forest model has less computation complexity (0.8 seconds of prediction)

hardware.evidence: Although our approach has low computational costs with an average prediction time of 0.5 seconds per packet capture (PCAP) file on baseline hardware (e.g., Intel i7-10700 CPU), its implementation within heterogeneous enterprise setups introduces additional practical concerns.
